title: Personal LLM experiments - mini tracker (2026)
content:
Mini experiment tracker (quick personal sheet)

Purpose:
- Keep a small, fast-to-scan record of tuning/serving experiments while iterating locally and on Redwood Dedicated.
- Capture perf + quality tradeoffs for prompts, quantization, and batching so I can pick settings for the next canary.

Columns: date | experiment_id | model | quant | batch | prompt_template | eval_set | metric (EM / avg_ll) | latency_ms | cost_per_1k_tokens | notes | next_steps

Entries:
2026-01-12 | exp-001 | redwood/llama-2-13b | int8 | 1 | few-shot-short | conv-eval-1 (500 msgs) | acc=0.62 / avg_ll=-1.95 | 210 ms | $0.24 | baseline run, default prompt, stable outputs but some tokenization issues on code tokens | try prompt variant with explicit code fences
2026-01-18 | exp-003 | redwood/llama-2-13b | int8 | 4 | few-shot-short | conv-eval-1 | acc=0.60 / avg_ll=-1.98 | 240 ms | $0.10 | batching reduces cost but slightly lower QA acc; likely context-window interference on examples | test dynamic batching with prefix caching
2026-01-22 | exp-007 | redwood/llama-2-13b | int4 | 1 | few-shot-short | conv-eval-1 | acc=0.58 / avg_ll=-2.20 | 170 ms | $0.12 | int4 drops quality but speeds up; hallucinations increased on numeric answers | schedule small eval on numeric subset
2026-02-02 | exp-011 | redwood/llama-2-70b | q4_0 | 1 | few-shot-short | conv-eval-1 | acc=0.68 / avg_ll=-1.45 | 540 ms | $1.40 | 70b much better on reasoning; cost is high - consider fallback policy for low-cost tier | prototype routing: 13b int4 for most, 70b for hard queries
2026-02-14 | exp-015 | redwood/llama-2-13b | int8 | 2 | few-shot-short + system instruction | conv-eval-1 | acc=0.64 / avg_ll=-1.88 | 225 ms | $0.14 | small gain from stronger system instruction; latency slightly up due to batch packing | lock prompt and run 3-day stability test

Quick notes / heuristics observed:
- Int8 seems the best balance for chat-like prompts on 13b for now. Int4 has useful speedups but requires extra eval on numbers.
- Batching helps cost but watch example ordering in prompt (static examples at start work better).
- For expensive models (70b) add routing with model-variant fallback to avoid overuse.
- Tokenization edge-cases on code: use explicit "```" fences and escape sequences in prompts.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Run numeric-heavy eval split for each quant profile (int8 vs int4) (ticket ENG-1421).
- [ ] Test prefix/KV caching impact on 13b int8 when batch>1 (measure cache hit rate vs latency).
- [ ] Decide rollback threshold for canary of new prompt: delta_acc < -0.03 OR avg_ll drop > 0.15.
- [ ] Add automated eval harness to run nightly on the small conv-eval-1 set and push metric diffs to CON-4523.

Links & refs:
- Quick convo eval set: gs://redwood-evals/conv-eval-1.csv (local copy used)
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-profiles/pull/87
- Jira: ENG-1421 (numeric eval), CON-4523 (prompt rollout)

Scratchpad (prompt variants):
- baseline: "You are an assistant. Answer concisely. Example: Q->A"
- system-strong: "You are a careful assistant. For numeric answers include calculation steps and final value in numeric form. Use code fences for any code."
- code-safe: "Wrap any code in triple backticks and explicitly label language."

Notes to self:
- Keep this file minimal - move stabilized configs to model-profiles once we lock them.
- When running Dedicated tests, include region tag and instance type in notes.

Last quick summary:
- current preferred: 13b int8, batch=1-2, system-strong prompt for sensitive numeric tasks; route to 70b for longform reasoning.
